# Local RHWP core build

This package starts from the upstream @rhwp/core 0.8.7 npm release and RHWP source tag v0.8.7 (commit 1a76570e833917d15817415a53c09ad61ab3203f). The local package version 0.8.7-hwp-editor.10 identifies the binary patches.

The patch adds format-independent logicalText and native page-number, total-page, and file-name field metadata to the header/footer query. It retains raw text and edit coordinates. A trailing automatic-number control is mapped back to its one-character placeholder in header/footer field metadata only; the generic paragraph coordinate model remains unchanged. Rust tests cover the metadata contract and the page-number/file-name template through HWP and HWPX round trips.

The bundled rhwp_bg.wasm was rebuilt from that source with the committed upstream Cargo.lock, Rust 1.93.1, and wasm-bindgen 0.2.127 (--target web). The JavaScript and TypeScript wrappers are copied from the upstream 0.8.7 npm release because the exported Rust method still returns JSON text.


The second local patch, paragraph-start-control-insertion.patch, keeps section/column controls at the paragraph head when text is inserted at logical offset zero before an inline control. Its Rust regression test verifies the raw control stream positions after insertion. The original package wrappers are unchanged.

The third local patch, body-format-batch-deferral.patch, makes body-paragraph character format, paragraph format and style application honour batch mode. Upstream's cell-paragraph mutators already defer their derived-state rebuild between beginBatch and endBatch, but applyCharFormat, applyParaFormat and applyStyle on body paragraphs still rebuilt resolved styles, recomposed the whole section and paginated on every call, so formatting N paragraphs cost N whole-section rebuilds. In batch mode these mutators now only record the section; endBatch resolves styles, recomposes each recorded section once and paginates. The whole section is recomposed (not only the touched paragraphs) because paragraph-shape and style changes can renumber later paragraphs. A Rust regression test applies reflowing character formatting, numbering and a style over a range with and without a batch and requires identical page counts and page SVG. The JavaScript and TypeScript wrappers produced by wasm-bindgen are byte-identical to the previous build; only rhwp_bg.wasm changed. Build: `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib`, then `wasm-bindgen --target web` on `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/rhwp.wasm`.

The fourth local patch, font-name-classification-memo.patch, is part of the same 0.8.7-hwp-editor.3 binary. Text measurement decides for every measured character whether the font is a KoPub face, by lowercasing the font name and searching it four times. Pagination re-measures every paragraph of the edited section, so on a 516-page generated document this classification was close to half the time of one typed character. The decision depends only on the name, so it is now made once per name. A Rust test compares the cached decision with the per-call test. Node + WASM insertText on the generated documents: medium about 80 -> 44 ms, large about 650 -> 240-390 ms measured back to back on the same machine.

The fifth local patch, offscreen-canvas-backend.patch, produces the 0.8.7-hwp-editor.4 binary. It adds `renderPageToOffscreenCanvas`, a typed OffscreenCanvas sibling of the upstream DOM Canvas renderer, so the document Worker can rasterize a page without a DOM. `scripts/patch-rhwp-offscreen.py <checkout>` generates `src/renderer/offscreen_canvas.rs` and `src/renderer/equation/offscreen_render.rs` from the upstream `web_canvas.rs` and `equation/canvas_render.rs` of the same checkout, so the drawing code is not maintained twice; the patch file records the remaining hand-visible changes (Cargo features, module declarations, the exported method). The generated files of the vendored build have SHA-256 406f83b1d9e7105f490448f796ff9ae3502ee6d250e9972883ad03ecd4e5ad05 and 3cb36ed55a9e71d4d666bd10c124a301f9aecf087438ae37226bfb82215523ec. The DOM renderer and `renderPageToCanvas` are unchanged; the script leaves the upstream doc comment of `renderPageToCanvas` on the new method, which only affects rhwp.d.ts comments.

The Worker backend never touches `window`, `document`, `HtmlImageElement` or a URL loader. Embedded raster pictures are decoded in Rust (`image`, now also gif/webp/ico) to RGBA and placed on an OffscreenCanvas; WMF/EMF/PCX/TIFF/EPS are converted locally and vector results are rasterized with resvg 0.47 with the image href resolver disabled. Limits: 8192 px per picture axis, 64 MiB decoder allocation, 16,777,216 px per rasterized vector picture, 64 MiB of decoded pictures per render call; the decoded-picture cache is cleared before and after every call. A picture that cannot be decoded within these rules, including a vector picture containing `<text>` (no font database is supplied), makes the call throw instead of returning a page with a silent hole. The plugin then shows that page through the unchanged SVG path.

Build of the fifth patch: apply the four earlier patches to tag v0.8.7, run the script, then `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib` with the checkout's pinned Rust 1.93.1 and `wasm-bindgen --target web` 0.2.127. Cargo.lock gains only the `image-webp` edge. rhwp.js, rhwp.d.ts and rhwp_bg.wasm.d.ts are the wasm-bindgen output of this build and differ from the upstream npm wrappers. rhwp_bg.wasm SHA-256: 5006a4f913eaf8d380ea650ee561ff16b604e43a89db2007bbeef5efeec4e586.

The sixth local patch, geometry-preserving-body-edit.patch, produces the 0.8.7-hwp-editor.5 binary. Upstream's body insertText and deleteText reflow only the edited paragraph but then repaginate the whole document on every call, so one typed character cost time proportional to the page count (about 5 ms at 11 pages, 50 ms at 103, 300 ms at 516) wherever the edit was. The patch records the paragraph's line segments before the edit and, when the reflow yields the same number of lines with identical vertical position, heights, baseline, spacing, column start, width and tag, recomposes only that paragraph and invalidates the page render cache; the section vpos pass and pagination are skipped. Only the UTF-16 line starts may differ. Everything else takes the unchanged upstream path: a paragraph that was not reflowed before in this session (no layout space metrics, or a dirty stored partition), a paragraph with controls, field ranges, a numbering marker or a control character, an empty paragraph before or after the edit, a render-normalized section, batch mode, and any dirty section or pending or deferred pagination. Edits that change the line count, cell edits and snapshot restore cost what they did.

The same patch replaces the HWPX space-width special case in `resolve_styles_for_document` (half-em only for 한양신명조 of 14 pt or more that occurs in body paragraphs and not in tables, found by scanning every paragraph) with the character-shape property: `useFontSpace` off means a half-em space, on keeps the font's own width. The rule and its PDF evidence come from the sibling project's docs/DECISIONS.md ("공백 한 칸은 반각"). On 77 HWPX files (the public fixtures and that project's samples, first 40 pages each) the text layout of every page is identical before and after, so this is a rule cleanup with no observed rendering change, not a measured fidelity gain.

A Rust regression test (`test_geometry_preserving_typing_matches_full_pagination`) types, grows and shrinks paragraphs through the normal path and through a batch, which always repaginates, and requires equal line segments, page counts and page SVG after every step. `scripts/verify-rhwp-incremental.mjs` does the same against the built package on 13 generated and public fixtures with seeded random edits, also comparing caret rectangles, line lookups and exported bytes; `scripts/benchmark-rhwp-core.mjs` measures the edit time. Build as for the fifth patch, with `--locked`; the wasm-bindgen wrappers are byte-identical to the previous build and only rhwp_bg.wasm changed. rhwp_bg.wasm SHA-256: 5cd8c3c224f0f2e367d468c8bed69a263b5f200ff0cb916cacbff460d3c126ae. Recovery records carry the engine version, so records written by 0.8.7-hwp-editor.4 are refused by this build and stay on disk.

The seventh local patch, double-slim-border-geometry.patch, produces the 0.8.7-hwp-editor.6 binary. Upstream drew a `DOUBLE_SLIM` (BorderLineType::Double) table, paragraph and diagonal border as two strokes of 0.3 x max(W, 3 px) separated by a gap of at least 1 px, so every double border was at least 3 px wide whatever its declared width. The patch uses the rule measured against Hancom output in the sibling project's docs/DECISIONS.md ("`DOUBLE_SLIM` 표 테두리와 공유 경계"): a declared width W is two strokes of W/4 whose centres are 3W/8 either side of the edge, so their outer edges span exactly W (0.7 mm -> 0.18 mm strokes 0.53 mm apart; 0.5 mm -> 0.12/0.37; 0.12 mm -> 0.03/0.08). `border_line_visual_span`, used only for page-border outsets, is unchanged. A Rust test (`double_slim_border_is_two_quarter_strokes_within_declared_width`) checks stroke width and offsets at 0.12, 0.5 and 0.7 mm; `tests/layout-rules-wasm.test.ts` checks the same envelope on generated 2x2 table documents (`scripts/prepare-layout-rules.mjs`, then `scripts/create-layout-rule-fixtures.py`) after HWPX and HWP round trips, including one stroke pair per shared cell edge. Build as for the sixth patch with `--locked`; the wasm-bindgen wrappers are byte-identical to the previous build and only rhwp_bg.wasm changed. rhwp_bg.wasm SHA-256: dde5ef5b674dc0c6a12d3a4acca8ba30aa7eebb7a02d2d3b949ca2a2cce5d85b. Records written by 0.8.7-hwp-editor.5 are refused by this build and stay on disk.

The eighth local patch, `textbox-storage-bit.patch`, is the IeumOffice backport of RHWP #8176, sourced from IeumOffice commit `98da0d6c4fd6ba1157bc16684e456a3f9e08e434`, Apache-2.0; its license and notice are distributed in `licenses/`. It keeps the HWP shape storage bit `0x01000000` in sync with the presence of a text box when one is created, attached or detached. Generated WASM regression `tests/hwp-textbox-storage.test.ts` reproduced the missing bit before the patch and checks both text boxes and ordinary rectangles afterwards.

The ninth patch, `style-attribute-propagation.patch`, is IeumOffice's patch 0013 from the same commit. It applies a new paragraph style while retaining individually overridden attributes, and propagates changes to styles through body paragraphs and nested document containers. `tests/style-parity-investigation.test.ts` reproduces the prior failure and tests both style application and updates in body and table cells. Build: apply the original seven patches (generate offscreen files using `scripts/patch-rhwp-offscreen.py`), then the eighth and ninth patches, `cargo +1.93.1 build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib --locked`, and `wasm-bindgen 0.2.127 --target web`. The JS and TypeScript wrappers are byte-identical to .6. The final `rhwp_bg.wasm` SHA-256 is `8a328e91ad2e9e5eb7ecb7d62f38f53d8355e579c0a38dc9cb3857669f1629ca`. Recovery journals from .6 remain on disk but cannot be replayed under .7; use the exact old runtime as in decision 54.

The tenth patch, `cell-paragraph-delete.patch`, provides `deleteParagraphInCellByPath`: it removes a paragraph without merging it into either neighbour, keeps the remaining paragraphs and their formatting, and recalculates cell positions. The existing merge-based approach changed the next paragraph's style when deleting the first paragraph. The plugin checks anchored content before calling it and leaves a required single paragraph empty. Apply this patch after the preceding nine; rebuild with the same cargo and wasm-bindgen commands. The generated JS and declarations add this one method, which remains internal to the plugin. The .8 WASM SHA-256 is `b13f37d2716570bb131f2189fd5ef137423f5dd4e7d73f79f8a543ea6eb19c03`. Journals from any older engine are retained and require their exact runtime as in decision 54.

The eleventh patch, `field-leading-offsets.patch`, fixes a leading-offset reconstruction error when a paragraph contains multiple fields. A leading empty field's END slot was counted as another control, moving a later field BEGIN before the first text character on HWPX export. The patch bounds the number of leading controls by the first field that actually starts later in the paragraph. Generated tests cover different and duplicate IDs, Unicode answers, ordinary edits, an inline shape, HWP/HWPX round trips and undo; the save-time field comparison remains as a separate guard. Build after all ten preceding patches using the same cargo and wasm-bindgen commands. The JS and TypeScript wrappers are byte-identical to .8. The .9 `rhwp_bg.wasm` SHA-256 is `3617ed11650ab05a3cfa50e4542173a0077a0f6db7ad29f486608784c70c6dbf`. Older recovery journals remain on disk and require their exact runtime.

The twelfth patch, `hwpx-placeholder-float-flow.patch`, produces 0.8.7-hwp-editor.10. Some HWPX generators store a single line at vertical position zero for every body paragraph, even when its text spans multiple lines. In a section with at least four such paragraphs and a PARA-relative top-and-bottom floating table, the patch reflows plain body and table-cell text using the existing line layout machinery before pagination. The calculated body flow and table placement then agree. Other sections retain their saved layout. A generated fixture checks text, table and subsequent text order and page bounds. On the reported document, read-only rendering moved the first table from above its preceding paragraph to a later page and reduced text glyphs outside page bounds from 12,209 to zero under Node font approximations; this is not a Hancom visual comparison. Apply after the prior eleven patches and rebuild with the commands above. The JS and TypeScript wrappers are unchanged. WASM SHA-256: `fc9fd97f8852ac285c1d36064c93348b49d5de7e71159835fef557c996a1cbc2`. Older recovery journals remain on disk and require their exact runtime.
